reviews.title: [release] Update safety: signature refusals, installer identity, settings repairs
reviews.summary: PR #46 (lane/release, 44 commits, 182 files) carries four own commits from 2026-10-14: T-293 publisher-signature refusals, its FIX-2 hardening (stop-once on unclear answers, refused installers keyed by SHA-256/signature with a cap of 20, bounded PowerShell read from System32, held read-only copy, Close on the stop card), council fixes B1 (one close listener), B2/FIX-1 (settings repair from the last good copy with timestamped set-asides) and F1 (installer HEAD only to GitHub hosts over https). The branch has no common ancestor with origin/main (merge-base fails; GitHub reports mergeable_state "dirty"), so it cannot land as is, and it would also clobber main's PLAN.md/STATE.md/PROVENANCE.md. Main already holds the whole T-293 + FIX-2 design in a stronger form in src-tauri/src/resources/update_guard.rs (Verdict::Retry, SIGNED_BUILD, 20 s SIGNATURE_LIMIT, GetSystemDirectoryW, HeldCopy with read-back, refusedInstallers keyed by sha256/signature, reset-only update_mark, plus the issuer pin AFTER 4 the branch left undone) with its wiring in update.rs:339-372 and the Close label in src/update/card.ts:254-262. B1 is in main (the single onCloseRequested listener lives in src/shell/useWindowSave.ts:69 with screenWriter.flush() before any await), B2 is covered by a different, council-chosen design (read falls back to .bak, corrupt file set aside under a unique timestamped name on save, never rewritten; T-441/T-075 tests), and F1 is covered by APP-070's public-only HEAD client (no local network, no https->http downgrade, capped hops) though without the GitHub host pin. The only small unique pieces (a structural one-listener test, salvaging still-parsing entries from a truncated file, GitHub host pinning and 410 for the installer probe) are optional improvements that conflict with or duplicate main's current doctrine, so the PR should be closed as superseded with those noted as follow-ups.

findings.title: No common ancestor with main; unmergeable and would overwrite main's plan/state files
findings.detail: `git merge-base origin/main origin/lane/release` exits 1 and GitHub reports mergeable=false, mergeable_state=dirty. The branch also edits PLAN.md, STATE.md, PROVENANCE.md and adds evidence/FIX-2.txt, a name main already uses for lane/look's FIX-2; landing it in any form would replace main's current task ledger and evidence with 2026-10-14 copies.
findings.fix: Close the PR; port nothing wholesale. Any wanted piece (see unique_work port plans) is re-applied by hand on a branch cut from 3af39cf3.

votes.reasoning:
The headline assertion ("no common ancestor with main") is an artifact of the local checkout, not a property of the PR. /home/user/kolux-rs is a shallow clone: `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints true and `.git/shallow` holds 11 commits, which are exactly the 11 "root" commits of origin/main (`git rev-list --max-parents=0 origin/main`; first-parent root is 53285e2d "APP-050 b2: arm the quit watchdog", a mid-build commit, not a repo origin). origin/lane/release was fetched in full down to the real root 7dad8dd2 "Kolux RS spec: the clean-room rebuild starts here" (787 commits, not in .git/shallow). So `git merge-base origin/main origin/lane/release` exits 1 only because main's true ancestry is cut off locally.

GitHub says otherwise, authoritatively: `gh api repos/TxaisX/kolux-rs/compare/main...lane/release` returns status "diverged", merge_base_commit 5f3b287035bc6d3ddc3f6c9727c11ca9c7862f5a (MERGE 66), ahead_by 44, behind_by 2161. The PR API (`pulls/46`) reports commits 44, changed_files 182, +7352/-415, base.sha 8e482af1 (which IS an ancestor of origin/main, exit 0). Locally `git rev-list --count origin/lane/release ^5f3b2870` = 44 and `git diff --stat 5f3b2870 origin/lane/release` = 182 files, +7352/-415: an exact match. The lane's own commit 5e6d7c71 "[release] merge main 5f3b287 into lane/release" records that base. A true unrelated-history branch would show 787 commits / 3065 files (that is what `git diff --stat origin/main origin/lane/release` shows locally: 3065 files, -289467 lines, which is the number the claim implicitly relies on).

"mergeable_state=dirty" is real but means ordinary content conflicts from being 2161 commits behind. A 3-way merge with the true base (`git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=5f3b2870 main lane/release`, run in a throwaway --shared clone in the scratchpad, main checkout untouched) conflicts in 51 files: content conflicts in DECISIONS.md, PLAN.md, PROVENANCE.md, STATE.md, scripts/release.mjs, src-tauri/src/{lib,state,update,git,files,projects,terminal,claude_accounts}.rs, src-tauri/src/cli/mod.rs (git rename-detects base cli.rs -> main cli/mod.rs), src/App.tsx and several editor/settings/update files; add/add conflicts in evidence/FIX-2.txt, evidence/T-293.txt, src-tauri/src/models.rs, src/crash.tsx, src/crash.test.ts, src/editor/autosave.ts, src/editor/autosave.test.ts.

The consequence claimed ("landing it in any form would replace main's current task ledger and evidence with 2026-10-14 copies") is therefore false for a merge or a rebase: PLAN.md/STATE.md/PROVENANCE.md are content conflicts and evidence/FIX-2.txt is an add/add conflict (main's is lane/look's FIX-2, the lane's is release's FIX-2, neither exists at base 5f3b2870: `git cat-file -e 5f3b2870:evidence/FIX-2.txt` fails). Git and GitHub stop on these; nothing is silently replaced. main's STATE.md line 6 reads "Done: 719 / 775 tasks · P0 cards passing: 209 / 228"; the lane's reads "Done: 422 / 660 · P0 6 / 228 · merge gate 49 waiting", and that stale ledger could only reach main through an explicit `-X theirs` resolution or a force-push, which is not a property of the PR. The file-name collision part of the claim is correct, but it is a conflict, not an overwrite; the claim also missed the second identical collision on evidence/T-293.txt.

What is true about PR #46, and what a correct write-up should say: it is a stale 44-commit lane whose two headline features already landed on main via other lanes. T-293 was built by lane/reliability on 2026-10-20 (origin/main:evidence/T-293.txt line 2) with the FIX-2 semantics ("refused" for good vs "stopped once", installers known by SHA-256 of their bytes) living in src-tauri/src/resources/update_guard.rs (Verdict::Stop vs Verdict::Retry lines 116-121, `vet(bytes, ...)` line 268, `pub struct Refused` line 283) and wired from src-tauri/src/update.rs lines 285-287 and 338-364. APP-048 settings repair landed as T-075 from lane/core on 2026-10-19 (main src-tauri/src/state.rs lines 142-374, PLAN.md line 80) with a different design from the lane's `repair_settings` (lane state.rs line 219). Of 5464 lane-added lines, 969 are verbatim in main; 100 of the 182 PR files are absent on main, 89 of them evidence files, and the source files absent by path are src-tauri/src/crash.rs, src-tauri/src/perms.rs, src/editor/session.ts(+test), src/lifecycle.ts(+test), src/projects/Cleanup.tsx, src/projects/cleanupScan.ts(+test), src/startup.test.ts (main has src/crash.tsx and src-tauri/src/lifecycle.rs, so even these need a function-level check before being called unique).
votes.corrected_fix:
1. Fix the measurement first: any local ancestry check in this container must run after `git fetch --unshallow` (or `git fetch --deepen=<n>` until `git merge-base origin/main origin/lane/release` prints 5f3b2870); otherwise every lane PR will be mis-graded as "no common ancestor". Cite GitHub's compare endpoint (merge base 5f3b2870, ahead 44, behind 2161) rather than the shallow-clone exit code.
2. Re-state the finding as: PR #46 is 2161 commits behind main and conflicts in 51 files (list above), with add/add collisions on evidence/FIX-2.txt and evidence/T-293.txt; its headline work (T-293 publisher stop + FIX-2 refused-by-bytes/stop-once, APP-048 settings repair) is already on main via lane/reliability (src-tauri/src/resources/update_guard.rs, src-tauri/src/update.rs 285-364) and lane/core (src-tauri/src/state.rs 142-374). Severity: not a blocker defect in the PR; it is a superseded, stale lane.
3. Disposition: either close #46 as superseded, or ask the lane owner to rebase onto 3af39cf3 dropping the update.rs/state.rs/ledger commits that main already has, renaming its evidence to the lane-prefixed names main uses (evidence/release-FIX-2.txt, evidence/release-T-293.txt, matching its existing evidence/release-FIX-1.txt) to remove the add/add collisions, and keeping only the pieces main lacks after a function-level check: src-tauri/src/crash.rs, src-tauri/src/perms.rs, src/editor/session.ts, src/lifecycle.ts, src/projects/Cleanup.tsx, src/projects/cleanupScan.ts and their tests. Hand-porting onto a branch cut from 3af39cf3 is an acceptable way to do that, but the reason given ("unmergeable, would overwrite main's ledger") must not be the one written in the report.

votes.reasoning:
The blocker is CONFIRMED on every point, reproduced directly against the fetched refs and in a throwaway worktree (created at scratchpad/wt-pr46-merge from origin/main, removed afterwards; main checkout verified clean at 3af39cf3, `git worktree list` shows only the main checkout).

1. No common ancestor. `git merge-base origin/main origin/lane/release` and `git merge-base --all ...` both exit 1 with no output. Root-commit sets are disjoint: lane/release (69b3dc54, 787 commits) has the single root 7dad8dd2; origin/main (3af39cf3) has 11 roots, none of them 7dad8dd2. The cause is a history rewrite on main: lane/release's own "merge main 5f3b287 into lane/release" commit (5e6d7c71) merged a main tip 5f3b2870 that `git merge-base --is-ancestor 5f3b2870 origin/main` says is no longer in main (exit 1); 5f3b2870 survives only on the other origin/lane/* branches.

2. Unmergeable, GitHub agrees. `gh api repos/TxaisX/kolux-rs/pulls/46` returns state=open, head=lane/release @ 69b3dc54, base=main, mergeable=false, mergeable_state="dirty", draft=false. In the worktree, `git merge --no-commit --no-ff origin/lane/release` fails with `fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories` (exit 128). Forcing it with `--allow-unrelated-histories` produces 417 conflicted files, including .gitattributes, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml, LOOP.md, DECISIONS.md, deny.toml, PLAN.md, STATE.md, PROVENANCE.md and evidence/FIX-2.txt, all in `AA` (both-added) status.

3. Would overwrite main's ledger with 2026-10-14 state. lane/release's tip is dated 2026-10-14 04:36 -0700; main's is 2026-10-31. `git diff --stat origin/main origin/lane/release -- PLAN.md STATE.md PROVENANCE.md evidence/FIX-2.txt` = 4043 insertions / 1048 deletions across the four files. The machine-written STATE.md `Done:` line (scripts/plan-check.mjs --write-state) on main reads "719 / 775 tasks · P0 cards passing: 209 / 228 · cutline 0 / 18 left · merge gate 0 waiting"; lane/release's reads "422 / 660 tasks · P0 cards passing: 6 / 228 · cutline 2 / 18 left · merge gate 49 waiting". PROVENANCE.md shrinks from 1114 to 675 lines. 270 task IDs ticked `[x]` in main's PLAN.md are not ticked in lane/release's PLAN.md. Taking the branch's copies of these files, by merge or by file-level port, regresses the ledger.

4. evidence/FIX-2.txt name collision is real. main's file begins "FIX-2 (lane/look, 2026-10-14): council re-review d2/look-829f533-rereview.md"; lane/release's begins "FIX-2 · council re-review of lane/release faa709d (FB 2, FS 3, AFTER 5) · 2026-10-14". Same path, two unrelated documents; the forced merge marks it AA.

Severity as a blocker holds: the PR cannot be merged by GitHub or by git without --allow-unrelated-histories, and the only way to force it yields 417 conflicts whose "resolution" would be to clobber main's current PLAN/STATE/PROVENANCE/evidence.
votes.corrected_fix: The proposed fix stands (close PR #46; land nothing wholesale; re-apply wanted pieces on a branch cut from 3af39cf3). One sharpening so the port is not guesswork: the branch's unique work is exactly the 41 non-merge commits in `git log --no-merges 5f3b2870..origin/lane/release` (c62bc689 T-100-b through 69b3dc54 FIX-2, all dated 2026-10-12..14). Port by cherry-picking those onto a branch from 3af39cf3 with the ledger files excluded (e.g. `git cherry-pick -n <sha>` then `git checkout 3af39cf3 -- PLAN.md STATE.md PROVENANCE.md evidence/` before committing), and rename the lane's evidence file to something like evidence/FIX-2-release.txt since evidence/FIX-2.txt on main belongs to lane/look. Because main moved 17 days past the lane's last merged main (5f3b2870), check each cherry-pick against what main already landed in the same files (src-tauri/src/update.rs, install.rs, state.rs, src/update/*, src/editor/*, src/projects/*, src/settings/*) before keeping it; several T-1xx items may already be on main under renumbered IDs. Never use `git merge --allow-unrelated-histories` for this branch: it yields 417 conflicts including CI workflows, deny.toml and LOOP.md.

findings.title: Refused installer is re-checked with Windows before the refused list is consulted, contrary to the comment
findings.detail: update_download runs check_publisher(&bytes) inside spawn_blocking first (up to SIGNATURE_LIMIT = 20 s, twice: own exe + held copy) and only afterwards tests refused_has(earlier, Some(&sha), ""). The comment at line 736-737 says an earlier-refused installer is 'stopped again without asking Windows'; it is asked every time, so a user with a remembered refusal pays the full signature read on each download of the same bytes.
findings.fix: Compute sha256 first, check refused_has before calling check_publisher, and only then spawn the signature read. (Main's wiring avoids the issue by filtering at check time by signature, update.rs:286-289.)

votes.reasoning:
The literal ordering is as described: on origin/lane/release (69b3dc54) src-tauri/src/update.rs:737-742 runs check_publisher(&bytes) inside spawn_blocking and only then (743-748) tests refused_has(earlier, Some(&sha), ""), while the comment at 735-736 (reviewer cites 736-737, off by one) says a refused installer is "stopped again without asking Windows". But the claimed failure scenario ("a user with a remembered refusal pays the full signature read on each download of the same bytes") is not reachable in the normal path, and when it is reachable the outcome is identical and the cost is one bounded read, not recurring:

1. A remembered refusal is stopped BEFORE any download at check time: update_check at update.rs:679-682 calls refused_has(list, None, &u.signature), returns Quiet::Refused with found=None, so pending becomes None (line 695). The front end only calls update_download after a check that found something (src/update/UpdateCenter.tsx:66), and after a Refuse the backend clears pending (update.rs:756), so a repeat update_download fails fast at line 721 ("There is no update to download") with no Windows call. The refused entry always carries the feed signature (line 753: signature: update.signature.clone()); tauri-plugin-updater 2.14.1 makes `signature` a required String that download() verifies (updater.rs:86, 901, 1893), so an empty-signature entry cannot be written; and both the key `update.refusedInstallers` and the comment were introduced in 69b3dc54 itself (git log -S), so no earlier build wrote sha-only entries.

2. The only way the sha branch at 744 fires is the same installer bytes served under a different minisign signature (the .sig carries a trusted comment with a timestamp, so re-signing identical bytes changes the string). Then Windows is asked once (bounded by SIGNATURE_LIMIT=20 s per read; typically seconds) AFTER the full installer download, which is unavoidable because the sha is only known once the bytes are in hand; the verdict is overridden to Refuse regardless of what Windows said (Allow/Unverified/Refuse all become Refuse, lines 744-748), and refused_add (lines 296-303) replaces the entry by sha with the NEW signature, so the next check stops it at check time again. So it is one extra bounded read per re-signing, not "each download of the same bytes", and the user-visible result is the same security-stop either way.

3. "Main's wiring avoids the issue" is wrong: main (3af39cf3) update.rs:286-289 filters at check time by signature exactly as the branch does, and main's update_download (308-369) plus resources/update_guard.rs vet() (268-278) consult no sha list at all — re-signed identical bytes on main are re-vetted by Windows on every download and are refused only if Windows answers definitively. The branch adds the sha override main lacks; its placement after the Windows read changes latency on a rare path, not correctness.

Net: a comment/code wording mismatch and a minor latency inefficiency on a rare path, not a major defect.
votes.corrected_fix: Not required for correctness. If anything is changed: either reword the comment at update.rs:735-736 to "An installer refused before is stopped again whatever Windows says this time" (matches the code), or, as a cheap tidy-up, read `earlier` from the store and compute `sha256_hex(&bytes)` before the spawn_blocking at 737 and return Verdict::Refuse("This installer was stopped earlier...") without calling check_publisher when refused_has(earlier, Some(&sha), "") is true, keeping the refused_add refresh at 752-755 so the new signature is recorded. Outcome is unchanged either way.

votes.reasoning:
The ordering the reviewer describes is literally present on origin/lane/release (69b3dc54) src-tauri/src/update.rs:737-746: spawn_blocking runs sha256_hex + check_publisher, and refused_has(earlier, Some(&sha), "") is tested only afterwards. But the claimed consequence ("a user with a remembered refusal pays the full signature read on each download of the same bytes") does not occur, and the comparison with main is wrong.

1. The PR branch has the same check-time filter the reviewer credits to main. update.rs:684-688 on the branch: `Ok(Some(u)) if refused_has(store.get(KEY_REFUSED).., None, &u.signature) => (None, Some(Quiet::Refused))`. That is the exact counterpart of main's update.rs:286-289. So after a remembered refusal, a re-check of the same installer sets `pending = None` and returns Quiet::Refused; nothing is downloaded and check_publisher is never reached.

2. The download command cannot be re-run on the same bytes without a new check. update_download reads `updates.pending` (line 721) and, on a Refuse, writes `pending = None` (line 756). Every subsequent call errors "There is no update to download; check again." before any download or signature read. The frontend matches: src/update/card.ts:179-182 turns a security stop into a `blocked` phase with no retry, and UpdateCenter.tsx only calls `update_download` after a check that returned `found` (line 66) or from retryDownload on a plain error phase.

3. Concrete demonstration (scratch crate built from the branch's verbatim Verdict/Refused/refused_has/refused_add/sha256_hex, driving the check->download->re-check sequence of lines 686 and 721-760; it compiled and ran): first refusal asks Windows once; "download w/o re-check" -> Err("There is no update to download"); "re-check, same feed" -> Quiet::Refused; three more check+download rounds -> Windows asked total still 1. The only route to the download-time sha check is the feed re-signing the SAME bytes with a new minisign signature: then Windows is asked once more, the final verdict is Refuse regardless of whether Windows says Allow/Unverified/Refuse (the override at 744-748 is unconditional, so reordering changes no verdict), refused_add replaces the entry with the new signature (line 754 via refused_add's retain-by-sha), and the next check filters it again. So the extra read happens at most once per re-signing, not per download.

4. The cost itself is overstated. SIGNATURE_LIMIT (20 s) is a kill deadline, not the typical duration of Get-AuthenticodeSignature. On an unsigned running copy (per the code's own note, "every release today, OD-03") check_publisher returns after the own-exe read only (line 452-455) and can never yield Refuse, so the refused list stays empty and the scenario cannot arise at all until signed builds ship; on non-Windows read_signer returns None and publisher_verdict returns Allow immediately.

5. Main has no download-time sha check at all (main update.rs:342-364 only records the sha on refusal); the PR's sha check is an added defense-in-depth layer on top of the identical check-time filter, not a regression from main.

What remains is a wording nit: the comment at lines 735-736 ("stopped again without asking Windows") is imprecise, since Windows' answer is ignored rather than not sought. That is not a major defect and the proposed reorder is at most an optional micro-optimization in a path reached once per re-signed installer.

No worktree was created (helpers were copied via git show); scratch build output was removed; main checkout untouched (git status clean, worktree list shows only the main checkout).
votes.corrected_fix: Downgrade to a comment nit / optional micro-optimization, not a defect. Either reword update.rs:735-736 to "An installer refused before is stopped again whatever Windows answers" or, if the small saving is wanted, compute `sha256_hex(&bytes)` and test `refused_has(earlier.as_deref(), Some(&sha), "")` before spawning check_publisher (skipping the signature read on a sha hit, which is only reachable when the feed has re-signed identical bytes). Behaviour and final verdict are unchanged either way; the check-time signature filter at update.rs:684-688 already prevents any re-download of a remembered installer.

findings.title: repair_settings rewrites a damaged settings.json at start, which main's council rule T-441 forbids
findings.detail: When settings.json fails to parse, the branch writes a rebuilt file over it (keeping .bad). The tombstone direction is right, but the proposal needs four corrections:

1. Do NOT add a `removed` field to library.json. The index is a bare JSON array: Library::read (artifacts.rs:333-335) deserializes Vec<Entry> and write (337-341) serializes &[Entry]. Use a sidecar file next to it (e.g. <dir>/removed.json holding a map origin -> (mtime_ms, size)), or an untagged-enum reader that accepts both shapes. The sidecar is simpler and safe.

2. Do not gate the tombstone on source == "workspace". A file inside <ws>/artifacts that was added by hand (Origin::hand, origin = the same absolute path) or captured from a Claude Write (DT-C58, origin = the file's own path) has the same origin key and is likewise re-imported as "workspace" after removal. 3. Take the stamp by stat'ing the origin at removal time: (modified_ms(path), metadata.len()). findings.title: artifacts_scan is a sync command: file copies and CDN fetches block the UI thread every 3 s
findings.detail: `#[tauri::command] pub fn artifacts_scan` runs on the window's thread (the repo's own rule, see agent_list_command.rs:1 and the comment on open_external at artifacts.rs:497; artifact_add is `async fn` + spawn_blocking for exactly this reason). The scan calls Library::add, which fs::copy's up to MAX_FILE = 100 MB per file and, for a page, runs fetch_script → tauri::async_runtime::block_on with a 20 s timeout per script, up to MAX_SCRIPTS = 16. Scenario: an agent writes report.html with three cdnjs scripts while the proxy is down → the UI freezes up to 60 s; a 90 MB mp4 landing in artifacts/ freezes the window for the copy; and the SCANNED mutex is held throughout, so a second window's scan waits too.
findings.fix: Make it `pub async fn artifacts_scan(app: tauri::AppHandle, path: String, project: Option<String>) -> Result<usize, String>` and wrap the body in `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || { ... }).await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?`, mirroring artifact_add at artifacts.rs:~486 (the AppHandle is Clone + Send). Also guard against overlapping scans: `try_lock()` the SCANNED mutex and return Ok(0) if busy, so the 3 s timer never queues behind a slow import.

findings.detail: scan_workspace sets Origin.at = file mtime. Library::add returns the existing entry early when `e.added > from.at`, so a file restored from a backup with cp -p / robocopy /COPY:DAT (older mtime, different content) is counted as changed (artifacts-changed is emitted, seen is updated) while the library keeps the stale copy forever. Probe test: rewrite a.html to <title>Restored</title>, set_modified(now-1h), scan returned n=1 but the title stayed "A".
findings.fix: In scan_workspace, use `at: now_ms()` for the Origin (the entry's `added` is 'when it was added', and it only has to be ≥ the file's mtime for the known-check at line 502), and change the known-check to compare the stored (mtime,size) instead of `added >= stamp.0`: store the file mtime in a new optional Entry field `modified: Option<u64>` (serde default) and compare `(e.modified, e.size) == stamp`.
